sentences.text: This small bird measured between 30 and 33 centimeters in length, excluding the tail feathers which are unknown.
Its skull possessed only a few teeth restricted to the anterior part of the mouth.
The tail feathers formed a graded, fan-like structure.
It possessed a rod-like pygostyle and lacked a long bony tail.
The first toe of the foot pointed backwards.
The reduced fingers suggest the animal may have had an alula.
The hand was far more advanced than that of Archaeopteryx, featuring three fingers with specific phalange counts and a carpometacarpus.
The arms were one and a half times longer than the legs, suggesting a large wing area.
The humerus was large and contained holes, apparently to reduce weight, similar to Confuciusornithidae.
The bird possessed gastralia but lacked uncinate processes, or these structures were not ossified.
A specimen contained numerous small gastroliths in its stomach, indicating a diet of plant seeds and fruits.
It was likely a glider or soarer that preferred open country but could perch on branches.
The first specimen was found in the summer of 2000 near Chaoyang City, Liaoning Province, China.
Sapeornis was discovered by the IVPP and reported in 2002 by scientists Zhonghe Zhou and Fucheng Zhang.
The genus name honors the Society of Avian Paleontology and Evolution combined with the Greek word for bird.
Two more nearly complete specimens were found about 40 km from the original site in the Dapingfang area.
Analysis of skeletal bones suggests Sapeornis had slow growth similar to Archaeopteryx, unlike the rapid growth of modern birds.
Evidence suggests Sapeornis was likely a herbivore that ate plant seeds and fruits, utilizing diverse food resources.
Not well adapted for flapping flight, Sapeornis was likely a glider preferring open environments, though capable of perching on branches.
Sapeornis belongs to the order Omnivoropterygiformes.
It belongs to the family Omnivoropterygidae.
Sapeornis is classified within the class Aves.
The species belongs to the parent group Pygostylia.
A 2012 study concluded that Didactylornis, Shenshiornis, and S. angustis are synonyms of Sapeornis chaoyangensis, while Omnivoropteryx is probably also another synonym.
Sapeornis lived during the early Cretaceous period, approximately 125 to 120 million years ago.
It lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
Character analysis demonstrates that Sapeornis was not closely related to Confuciusornis despite sharing some derived features.
